posts.text: 🇮🇱 🗣 Netanyahu insists most Israelis back unity government as he battles for his freedom 🔊 “There is a desire to reach agreements that will put an end to the division among us,” the Israeli caretaker prime minister said Monday, urging both sides to be “flexible” to secure a working deal. Monday saw the eighth day of talks between Netanyahu’s Likud and Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar opposition on a potential unity government deal after neither side proved able to secure enough support to form a workable coalition on their own following October’s vote. Eisenkot previously got the endorsement of Israel’s Arab minority parties, but other opposition parties, including Avigdor Liberman’s Yisrael Beytenu, Naftali Bennett’s B’Yachad and Yair Lapid’s Yesh Atid ruled out the idea . The Times of Israel reported last week that Likud insists on Netanyahu staying on as PM without any rotation, and that opposition coalition parties would have to pledge full support for another round of fighting with Iran. If a new government can’t be cobbled together by December, the Knesset will dissolve and Israelis will be asked to go to the polls again in early 2027. Israel has had five deadlocked elections and short-lived governments in seven years, with the political instability and criminal corruption trials threatening Netanyahu with prison widely believed to have played a role in his particularly hawkish foreign policy over the last three years. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime

📡 Russia’s Medvedev slams US double standards on Iran’s nuclear program 📌 Moscow, IRNA – Deputy chairman of the Russian Security Council strongly criticized the US for its contradictory and hypocritical approach to Iran’s nuclear program. In an article titled “State Sovereignty and Nuclear Weapons: International Legal Aspects of Ensuring National Security” for the Moscow Journal of International Law, Dmitry Medvedev argued that appeals to the nuclear non-proliferation regime are frequently invoked for political purposes, disregarding the reality on the ground. ​ Medvedev pointed out that Washington attacked Iran under the pretext of defending the non-proliferation regime, despite Tehran’s clear commitment to its obligations. ​ “Through its complete openness to negotiations and inspections in the field of peaceful nuclear energy, Tehran has demonstrated, not in words but in deeds, that it has no desire to possess nuclear weapons. And even in the face of direct threats of nuclear bombardment and aggression, including against civilian nuclear facilities, the Iranians have not yet renounced their status as a non-nuclear state under the NPT,” he stated. ​ The Russian official emphasized that Washington’s actions “demonstrate the double standards of American non-proliferation policy and are driven exclusively by geopolitical considerations: restrictions are imposed on unfriendly states.” ​ Elsewhere in the article, the Russian official pointed to the NPT and stated that the text of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation is self-sufficient. However, the document’s status undermines its enforcement, which depends on the degree of loyalty of one of the great powers: “The universality of the NPT is gradually being eroded, not by any flaws in the treaty's text, but by the uneven nature of its political application.” ​ “When the scope of permissible nuclear activities effectively depends on whether a state is an adversary or an ally of a major power or a military bloc, the non-proliferation regime loses some of its normative persuasiveness. Formally, the law remains uniform, but political practice makes its application selective.” ​ Withdrawal from the NPT automatically frees countries of their non-proliferation obligations: “A state’s withdrawal from the NPT removes its responsibility under international law for developing nuclear weapons,” Medvedev added. 📲 @Irna_en ​

Scammers send fake court summons to Russians Fraudsters are distributing counterfeit judicial notices via messengers, using intimidation to force victims to call them. Users receive a message demanding their presence in court and urging them to open a PDF titled 'Decision'. Clicking the link launches a site that requests a six-digit code, mimicking legitimate authorisation services but generating the code internally. After entering the code, users receive a notification that their state service account has been hacked. They are then pressured to urgently contact a supposed support line. The scammers' goal is to make the victim initiate the call, leading to blackmail, coercion into sabotage, or other criminal activities. @Slavyangrad
